title: Nathan Fielder Tells Us Everything
gist: WIRED cover interview with Nathan Fielder about his secret documentary on Elizabeth Holmes and Billy Evans, covering the unplanned production, his view of Silicon Valley's tolerance for lying, and a closing call from Holmes saying 'I trust you'. Mostly culture, with a few Silicon Valley takeaways.

insights.claim: Fielder argues Silicon Valley culture normalizes lying, with founders faking it and VCs expecting it, and that Holmes did the same thing as other founders to the nth degree.
insights.speaker: Nathan Fielder
insights.so_what: Frames Theranos as extreme end of a norm rather than an anomaly.

insights.claim: Fielder asserts Elon Musk lies to the public, regulators, lawmakers, investors and shareholders.
insights.speaker: Nathan Fielder
insights.so_what: Opinion from a comedian, not a documented claim in the article.
insights.quote: Elon Musk is an incredible liar

insights.claim: Drummond reports that after reading back on Holmes she felt less empathy than on first viewing, showing how reporting reframes sympathetic portrayals.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: Narrative of the fraudster shifts with context.
insights.quote: felt like such a fucking dupe

insights.claim: The film was kept secret for three years with only a few dozen people aware, and A24 chose a surprise Telluride debut about five weeks before release.
insights.speaker: Nathan Fielder
insights.so_what: Surprise-launch marketing generated heavy online buzz.

insights.claim: Fielder and Lance Oppenheim were able to deliver nothing to A24 if the project failed, which Fielder says freed him from the pressure to produce.
insights.speaker: Nathan Fielder
insights.so_what: Low-commitment development allowed an unscripted outcome.
insights.quote: we need the ability to deliver nothing to you guys

insights.claim: Holmes and Evans approached A24 to have their life documented, and Fielder then asked A24 to meet her; shooting spanned a 34-day period before her incarceration.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond
insights.so_what: Subjects solicited the documentary, an unusual reputation-management attempt.
insights.locator: A bit of a both thing

insights.claim: Fielder says he began without intending to appear on camera but concluded someone had to push back on what he saw as propaganda from the couple.
insights.speaker: Katie Drummond

insights.claim: Fielder says the production cut off communication with Evans near the end because of increased efforts to control the project.
insights.speaker: Nathan Fielder
insights.quote: increased effort, we felt, to control the process

insights.claim: Holmes called Fielder from prison after more than six months of silence and twice said 'I trust you'.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Holmes
insights.so_what: Ongoing contact complicates the film's ambiguity.

insights.claim: Fielder says that no one involved, including his editor, can agree on why Holmes and Evans wanted him there or on their relationship.
insights.speaker: Nathan Fielder
insights.so_what: The film is deliberately ambiguous and may drive debate.
insights.quote: This is a question that we are still debating to this day.
